source_claim: For I⊆{1,…,n−1}, the complement Δ\I is the set of block cut positions c_j=a₁+⋯+a_j for a composition a₁+⋯+a_s=n with each a_i≥1. P_I is the stabilizer in GL_n of the coordinate partial flag 0⊂k^{a₁}⊂k^{a₁+a₂}⊂⋯⊂k^n, equivalently the block upper-triangular matrices with block sizes a_i. Its Levi is ∏GL_{a_i}, its unipotent radical is block upper unitriangular, and the parabolic is their semidirect product. The general P_I is the intersection of the single-cut stabilizers over cuts in Δ\I, not over I.

Beside it, partition an n×n matrix into diagonal blocks of sizes a₁,…,a_s; show arbitrary diagonal blocks, arbitrary blocks above the block diagonal, and zero blocks below. Label the invertible block-upper-triangular stabilizer P_I.
Mark the cut set {c₁,…,c_{s−1}}=Δ\I. Show the general stabilizer as the intersection of single-cut stabilizers for these cuts, not for indices in I.
Optionally label the diagonal block subgroup L_I=∏_j GL_{a_j} and the block upper-unitriangular subgroup R_u(P_I), with the multiplication R_u(P_I)⋊L_I→P_I.
mathematical_checks: Require a_i≥1 and ∑a_i=n; each cut c_j is strictly increasing and lies in {1,…,n−1} for j<s.
Under the source convention Δ\I equals the cut set of partial sums. Do not substitute I for its complement when indexing the flag or taking the intersection of single-cut stabilizers.

A matrix preserves the standard coordinate flag exactly when its blocks below the diagonal vanish; the diagonal blocks must be invertible for membership in GL_n, and entries above the block diagonal are arbitrary.
The Levi consists of the invertible block-diagonal matrices; the unipotent radical has identity diagonal blocks, zero blocks below, and arbitrary blocks above.
Boundary checks: the composition (1,…,1) gives all cuts, I=∅ and P_I=B; the one-part composition (n) gives no cuts, I=Δ and P_I=G. For n=1, both coincide with G=B=G_m.

source_lines.text: For $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n-1\}$ let $\Delta\smallsetminus I=\{a_1,a_1+a_2,\dots,a_1+\cdots+a_{s-1}\}$ with $a_i\ge1$ and $\sum a_i=n$; then $P_I$ consists of the block upper triangular matrices with diagonal blocks of sizes $a_1,\dots,a_s$, arbitrary entries above the block diagonal and zero below, the standard Levi subgroup is $L_I=\prod_i\mathrm{GL}_{a_i}$ (block diagonal) and $R_u(P_I)$ is the block upper unitriangular subgroup, with identity diagonal blocks, zero blocks below them and arbitrary blocks above them; the multiplication $R_u(P_I)\rtimes L_I\to P_I$ is an isomorphism, $I\mapsto P_I$ is a bijection onto the smooth parabolic subgroup varieties containing $B$, and $P_\varnothing=B$, $P_{\Delta}=G$.

Thus $P_I$ is the group of invertible matrices preserving the flag of subspaces $0\subseteq k^{a_1}\subseteq k^{a_1+a_2}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq k^n$, i.e. the block upper triangular matrices with diagonal blocks of sizes $a_1,\dots,a_s$; its unipotent radical $R_u(P_I)$ has identity diagonal blocks, zeros below and arbitrary blocks above and its Levi factor is the block diagonal $\prod_i\mathrm{GL}_{a_i}$; the multiplication map $R_u(P_I)\rtimes L_I\to P_I$ is a group-scheme isomorphism by [F2]

The maximal proper parabolics correspond to $I=\Delta\smallsetminus\{i\}$, i.e. to the stabilizers of a single subspace of dimension $i$: taking $a_1=i$, $a_2=n-i$ gives the block upper triangular group with two diagonal blocks, which is the stabilizer of $k^i\subseteq k^n$, and the general $P_I$ is the intersection of these stabilizers over the cuts $i\in\Delta\smallsetminus I$, not over $I$.
